# How to Create a Home Maintenance Binder for Your Manufactured Home + Free Guide


Published On: September 25, 2026


•


2 min read


•


### **Keeping up with home maintenance is easy when your paperwork and checklists are stored in one place. Download your FREE Cavco Home Maintenance Guide to get started.**


Owning a manufactured home comes with many responsibilities, including keeping up with regular and seasonal maintenance tasks. Ongoing maintenance helps protect your investment, keeps systems running efficiently and prevents small, avoidable issues from becoming costly repairs.


Create your own home maintenance binder by downloading and printing the free Cavco Home Maintenance Guide below.


### Step 1: Gather home-related documents


Start by collecting the most important documents related to your Cavco manufactured or modular home. These may include:


- Home purchase documents
- Closing paperwork
- Insurance policies
- Property surveys
- Manufacturer information
- HUD certification information
- Financing documents
- Community or land lease agreements, if applicable
- Any other documents relating to the purchase of your home


### Step 2: Choose Your Binder Format


Decide how you want to organize your information. Most Cavco homeowners prefer to use a traditional three-ring binder with tabbed sections, while others choose to also keep information organized in a digital folder stored on a computer or cloud service.


Many homeowners find that a physical binder is especially useful because it can be stored in a central location and easily referenced during maintenance projects or service appointments.


[Download and print your FREE Cavco Home Maintenance Guide](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/26_Cavco-Home-Maintenance-Binder_FINAL-1.pdf)


### Step 3: Download and print the FREE Cavco Home Maintenance Guide and Create Your Binder.


## What’s Inside the Cavco Home Maintenance Guide?


The guide includes a **home maintenance schedule** where you can keep track of monthly, seasonal and annual tasks, such as changing HVAC filters, testing smoke alarms, inspecting the roof and gutters, checking exterior caulking and more.


It also includes space to **record repairs and service visits** , so you can keep track of when work was completed, who performed it, what it cost and any related warranty information. You’ll also have sections for **appliance and system information** , making it easier to keep all of your warranties and manuals together.


Your binder can also become a handy place to keep **important contacts and home improvement records** . Store information for your retailer, insurance provider, utility companies and service contractors, along with receipts, contractor invoices, product information, paint colors and photos from home improvement projects.


With the right maintenance routine and a little planning, you can help protect your home, prevent problems and enjoy it for years to come.
